venture.name: Golf Ball Locator
venture.name_status: Working product label in supplied PDF; separate business name not specified
venture.concept: A golf ball paired with an intuitive mobile app to make lost balls easier to find.
venture.primary_product: Proposed smart golf ball with app-based location and an audible signal
venture.target_customers: U.S. golfers, from teenagers through older adults, of any gender; the PDF describes upper-middle-income customers or below.
customer_needs: Acceptable ball feel and playing performance
venture.value_proposition: Help golfers locate balls quickly and spend more time enjoying golf.
venture.geographic_market: United States primary; Europe and Asia mentioned as possible future markets
venture.distribution_channels: Course, club professional and pro-shop partnerships proposed in the PDF; sales channels not finalized.
features: Proposed one-tap Find My Ball control
venture.source: Dalton Ochab.pdf, entire document reviewed; venture statement on page 1 and later research applications
assumptions: Direct online sale is a pricing scenario, not a confirmed distribution decision.
Benchmark proposed integrated smart balls; no separate receiver assumed in the tentative price.
Audible signal and simple app use are proposed features; technical performance is unproven.
missing_details: Final pack sizes and launch channels

competitors.name: Chiping
competitors.geographic_market: United States storefront; worldwide shipping advertised
competitors.target_customers: Golfers seeking app-assisted ball recovery, including technology-oriented recreational golfers (analyst interpretation)
competitors.primary_products: App-connected smart golf balls in 6- and 12-ball sets
differentiating_features: BLE connection to phone; GPS used in app rather than inside ball
competitors.relevance: Closest observed match to a ball and phone system for finding a lost ball.
competitors.operating_evidence: Active US storefront with product listings and cart controls; fulfillment not tested and stock indicators conflict.

competitors.name: Callaway
competitors.geographic_market: United States prices used; international brand
competitors.target_customers: Recreational golfers seeking soft feel, distance and colored ball options (analyst interpretation)
competitors.primary_products: Supersoft Yellow and Supersoft Matte Green golf balls
competitors.positioning: Budget alternative within this selected sample
competitors.relevance: A golfer may choose a low-cost colored ball rather than pay for electronic recovery.
competitors.operating_evidence: Official US product pages show In Stock and Add To Cart.

competitors.name: Volvik
competitors.target_customers: Golfers with moderate swing speeds who value soft feel and high visibility
competitors.primary_products: Vivid Soft matte golf balls, including quantity bundles
competitors.positioning: Mid-market visibility alternative within this sample
competitors.relevance: Directly addresses easier tracking and finding through visual contrast rather than electronics.
competitors.operating_evidence: Active current product page with Add to cart and quantity tiers; variant stock not independently confirmed.

groups.note: One representative offer per competitor; no demand weighting. Smart group has one observation and no cross-brand distribution.
One representative offer per competitor; no demand weighting. Smart group has one observation and no cross-brand distribution.

comparison.normalization: Current pack price / balls in pack; multiply by 12 for dozen equivalent. Equivalent unit prices are not actual separately offered pack prices. No pooled average across smart and conventional groups.

market_opportunities.observation: Large price gap between Chiping smart balls and conventional visibility balls.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Test an intermediate smart-ball price and a small trial pack; the gap alone does not prove unmet demand.

market_opportunities.observation: Conventional alternatives emphasize color, soft feel and playing performance.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Demonstrate comparable feel and distance while showing recovery in rough; add bright colors as an optional feature.

market_opportunities.observation: The PDF proposes a simple Find My Ball control; its simulated focus group raised usability concerns.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Prototype one-tap pairing and an optional audible alert, then test with real golfers. Simulated opinions are hypotheses.

market_opportunities.observation: Volvik uses quantity bundles; Chiping has larger pack savings.
market_opportunities.interpretation: Consider a three-ball starter pack and later replacement packs. Quote customization separately after its cost is known.

preliminary_pricing_recommendation.status: Preliminary analyst recommendation, not an observed competitor price
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.pricing_model: One-time purchase with basic locator app included at no extra subscription charge (proposed)
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.rationale: Test below Chiping at $33.325 per ball for Starter and $31.6625 for Expert, but above conventional visibility balls. A smaller three-ball pack lowers initial commitment. A simple audible search function and demonstrated ball performance would need to justify the premium.
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.position: About 40-55% below Chiping Starter per ball; roughly 5-9 times the selected conventional representative per-ball prices.
preliminary_pricing_recommendation.uncertainties: Cost feasibility, demand, durability, reliable recovery in rough, battery life, signal range, conformance and app support remain unknown. Competitor evidence alone cannot establish an optimal price.

research_limitations: Three relevant brands and seven selected pricing offers form a purposive sample, not a complete market census. No market-share or demand weighting.
Listed prices checked October 27, 2026. No purchase or checkout performed. Inventory, tax, shipping, codes and color availability can change.
Chiping price is verified but inventory is uncertain because storefront output includes both sold-out and cart controls. Active storefront does not establish fulfillment reliability.
Manufacturer performance claims were not independently tested. No claim that any ball can always be recovered, particularly in water.
Chiping FAQ states BLE, app GPS, approximately 30 yards/meters (wording is ambiguous), nonrechargeable battery and no submitted official conformance ruling; do not infer tournament approval.
Conventional visibility balls and smart locator balls are functionally different. Statistics are reported separately even after quantity normalization.
Blank workbook prices and JSON null mean not established or not separately listed, never zero. Displayed regular comparison prices are not verified historical prices.
Volvik quantity offers are recorded as promotional bundle prices with no confirmed end date. Its stated 10% and 17% savings are rounded.
Customization prices were not captured. No separate paid subscription observed for these researched offers; this does not prove no other charges exist.

The PDF has a broad income and age definition, no finalized company name or technical specifications, and a 39-versus-38 retail-observation count discrepancy. Its AI focus group is fictional and does not validate human demand.
